newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds propelled by short-squeeze, still eye 100.
newsitem.headline: Bunds propelled by short-squeeze, still eye 100.

text.p: Bunds firmed in late trade amid short-covering and are expected to touch 100 this week, but dealers said they were unsettled by Monday's half-point drop and were growing sceptical about how long the rally would last.
December Bund futures were quoted at 99.66 at 1435 GMT, up 40 basis points from Monday's close.
Dealers said the rally was caused by the strength of support around the session low of 99.15 which prompted dealers to close short positions opened during Monday's sharp fall.
"We keep seeing bear traps here, we're definitely going to see 100, every one wants to see it."

Another dealer said, "I was in a bullish mood, but Monday's fall was confusing. I still think Bunds will hit 100 this week but the market is futures-led. Investors in the cash Bund market are afraid to buy at these levels."
Dealers said German jobless figures released in the morning had little impact on the market.
The pan-German seasonally-adjusted jobless total rose by 39,000 to 3.991 million in September while the unemployment rate, based on unadjusted data, eased slightly to 10.1 percent from 10.2 percent.
Economists said the data were a setback for hopes that the economy was gaining momentum. Dealers said the data had little impact because they amounted to no surprise.

Meanwhile, news that German engineering union IG Metall demanded a wage increase of 4.5 to 5.0 percent had little impact on the market, dealers said. IG Metall said it was prepared to accept part of the rise in the form of job security measures.
